lines.text: If you pop a party popper at a birthday, congrats, you just built a fireworks show.
But it's one tiny pop, a puff of confetti, and the whole town is watching.
So licensed pros pack it into a paper ball called a shell, lower it into a mortar tube, and a lift charge underneath shoots it sky-high.
Now it flies, until it bursts too low, right above the crew's hard hats.
So they add a time fuse that burns on the way up, and fires the burst charge near the top.
But it's just a white flash and a bang: no color, no shape, no "wow".
So they fill it with pellets called stars, made with metal salts: strontium burns red, barium green, copper blue. Arrange them in a heart, and the sky draws a heart. Sometimes sideways.
Now it's gorgeous, until someone has to light a thousand fuses by hand. Goodbye, eyebrows.
So they wire an electric match to every shell, and a computer far away fires each one seconds early, so it bursts right on the beat.
But before you look up, follow, because next we're building a bank vault.
Now just add music, a crowd far, far back, and one guy who claps too early.
One button, a thousand shells, zero eyebrows lost.
And congrats, you just built a fireworks show yourself.
And the dog? Under the bed until Tuesday.
